patient_name_source.text: A 66-year-old female with knee osteoarthrosis who failed conservative management.

discharge_date_source.text: She was felt to be ready for discharge home on 03/19/2007.

procedures_performed: Mechanical and chemical deep venous thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis were initiated.
Hemovac drain was discontinued on postoperative day #2.
Continuous passive motion (CPM) was also initiated.

source.text: Prescriptions were written for Percocet and Coumadin.
Prescriptions were written for Percocet and Coumadin.
Follow up with Dr. X in one week.

diagnosis_explanation: Your knee has arthritis. This means the smooth covering on the ends of your bones has worn away. This can cause pain and stiffness in your knee.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and have some pain.
- Rest often but try to move your leg a little.
- Keep your surgical leg elevated when you sit.
- Do not put more than 50% of your weight on your right leg.
- You can eat normally.
- Your goal is to do your physical therapy exercises daily.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101°F.
- Call your doctor if you have increased redness or swelling.

**Week 2:**
- Your pain may start to get a little better.
- You can walk short distances inside your home.
- Continue to use crutches or a walker as advised.
- Do not put more than 50% of your weight on your right leg.
- Keep eating healthy foods.
- Your goal is to increase your walking time slightly each day.
- Call your doctor if your calf pain or swelling gets worse.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel more energy and less pain.
- You can walk a bit farther and may use one crutch.
- You can start to put more weight on your right leg.
- You can bend your knee a little more each day.
- Keep up with your physical therapy.
- Your goal is to walk around your home without help for short periods.
- Call your doctor if your surgical wound opens up.

**Week 4:**
- Your knee should feel less stiff and painful.
- You can walk without crutches for short distances.
- You may be able to walk up and down one flight of stairs.
- You can start to do light chores around the house.
- Ask your doctor before you start driving again.
- Your goal is to walk for 15 minutes outside your home.
- Call your doctor if you have sudden trouble breathing or chest pain.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people feel much better within 4 to 6 weeks.
- Keep doing your exercises every day.
- You can gradually return to normal activities.
- Healing takes time, so be patient with yourself.
- Follow up with your doctor as scheduled.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Questions about your pain medicine: Your doctor can help you plan.
- Knee pain is getting worse: Your doctor needs to know.
- You have trouble walking: Your doctor needs to check this.
- Wound healing slow: Your doctor needs to check this.
- Mild knee swelling: This can happen while you heal.
- Redness around your knee: This can mean infection.
- You feel very tired: This can mean problems.
